clue.text: Ted and Oscar reuniting old soldiers

indicators.note: bringing the two names together again in a new order signals that their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Two old friends, Ted and Oscar, meet up again with some veterans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reuniting' shuffles the eight letters of TED and OSCAR together.
explanation.definitionFit: British soldiers of earlier centuries were nicknamed for their scarlet tunics.

clue.text: Say no to garbage

explanation.surface: Turning down rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to decline, and the noun, stressed differently, means household waste.

clue.text: Locomotive passes on American railroad

parts.note: to pass on is to die
the el is an elevated railway in American cities

explanation.surface: A train engine passes along an American line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passes on' looks like 'goes by' but means dies; the EL is the elevated railway in Chicago or New York.
explanation.definitionFit: A diesel is a railway engine driven by a diesel motor.

clue.text: Soldiers rebuked for bloomer

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
chid is an old past tense of chide, to rebuke

explanation.surface: Soldiers were told off for making a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a blunder, but here is something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is a flowering plant, and an orchid is one with showy flowers.

clue.text: Present chief, for example — frequently he would appear in novel or film

parts.note: being present is being there
chief means main

indicators.note: to appear in something is to be inside it, so these pieces go within the other

parts.note: say means for example
oft is an old word for often
he would contracts to he'd

explanation.surface: A tribute to a leading figure who often turns up in books and films.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appear in' sets the frequent visitor and his contraction inside the example word; the long phrase 'Present chief' reads as a tribute, but it splits into two plain synonyms.
explanation.definitionFit: Kazuo Ishiguro's Booker-winning novel about a butler was filmed by Merchant Ivory in 1993.

clue.text: Extremely troublesome component of revolving door must be fixed

indicators.note: becoming a component of something means going inside it, so one piece sits within the other
a revolving thing turns round, so the word door is read backwards
the extreme letters of a word are its first and last, here of troublesome

explanation.surface: A faulty part in a revolving door needs repairing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolving' makes ROOD; 'component of' sets the troublesome ends inside, while 'Extremely' poses as an intensifier. 'must be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rooted is firmly fixed in place, like a plant held by its roots.

clue.text: See 4
Office worker, former model

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker
late means former, as in the late president

explanation.surface: A secretary who used to be a fashion model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' looks like a catwalk model, but means a pattern to copy.
explanation.definitionFit: A template is a pattern or model used as a guide for making copies.

clue.text: Seaman with two sets of cards

parts.note: a deck is a full pack of cards
a hand is the set of cards dealt to one player

explanation.surface: A sailor carrying two packs of playing cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two sets of cards' gives two pieces: DECK and HAND.
explanation.definitionFit: A deckhand is a sailor who works on the deck of a ship.

clue.text: Christian name of producer for "The Archers"?

definitions.meaning: ... Christian led the mutiny on the Bounty, so this is the given name of a man surnamed Christian
a maker of arrows supplies people who shoot with bows

explanation.surface: A quiz question about the name of the producer of a long-running radio soap.
explanation.walkthrough: The Archers is a long-running BBC radio soap about country life; read literally, archers are bowmen. 'Christian name' looks like 'first name' but means the forename of Fletcher Christian.
explanation.definitionFit: A fletcher is an arrow-maker, the trade that equips bowmen; it is also the mutineer Christian's forename.

clue.text: Geometry I can deploy for derivation of power

indicators.note: to deploy is to arrange or spread out into position, so these letters are set out afresh

explanation.surface: Mathematical tools put to use in working out where power comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deploy' rearranges the twelve letters of GEOMETRY, I and CAN; 'for derivation of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuclear power from splitting atoms is a form of power generation, so this phrase names a kind of power.

clue.text: Representative providing derogatory description of person

definitions.meaning: an example that represents its class, such as a sample taken for testing
a nasty or sorry example of a human being, as in 'a poor example of a man'

explanation.surface: A political representative being described in insulting terms.
explanation.definitionFit: A typical sample is a representative example, and 'a nasty one' is a sneering way of describing someone.

clue.text: Means of breaking the law

indicators.note: something broken comes apart, so the letters of the words are taken apart and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Asking how someone came to break the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' rearranges THE LAW; 'of' is a link. 'Means' looks like a verb or 'method' but is the noun for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's means are their money and resources, which is the same as their riches.

clue.text: Printer's employee being kind to dog

parts.note: a type is a kind or sort
a setter is a breed of gun dog

explanation.surface: A print-shop worker being nice to a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kind' looks like an adjective meaning nice, but it is the noun 'sort'.
explanation.definitionFit: A typesetter arranges type for printing, so works for a printer.

clue.text: Romany wry about Simpson in Victorian novel

indicators.note: one piece goes round the other, so the cartoon name sits inside
wry can mean twisted or bent, so the word Romany is twisted into a new order

parts.note: Bart Simpson is the cartoon son in The Simpsons

explanation.surface: A Gypsy with a wry look, regarding a man named Simpson, in a nineteenth-century book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wry' makes MARYON and 'about' wraps it round the cartoon boy; Romany looks like the novel's subject, but is only fodder. Elizabeth Gaskell wrote the book.
explanation.definitionFit: Elizabeth Gaskell's first novel, published in 1848, is set among Manchester mill workers in Victoria's reign.

clue.text: European head of state entertained by college student

indicators.note: a guest entertained is taken in, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: an Etonian is a pupil at Eton College

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here of state

explanation.surface: A national leader is hosted by a schoolboy from an elite college.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is a famous English boarding school; 'entertained by' puts S inside ETONIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Estonia, a Baltic country, is a European.

clue.text: Worshipper with faint heart — irregular soldier

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letter, here of faint
irregular means not in order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A faint-hearted worshipper is described as a soldier in an irregular force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faint heart' gives I, the middle letter of 'faint'; 'irregular' mixes it with SOLDIER. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who idolises adores and reveres, as a devotee does.

clue.text: Siegfried, initially pale, has a reddish hue in ballet

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word Siegfried

parts.note: wan means pale
lake is a crimson pigment

explanation.surface: The prince Siegfried looks pale and then flushes in a ballet.
explanation.walkthrough: Siegfried is the prince in this very ballet. 'has a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tchaikovsky's ballet about Odette, a princess turned into a bird.

clue.text: Snake in the grass is about to admit flatulence

indicators.note: admitting something lets it in, so one piece goes inside the other
turned about means faced the other way, so the words are read backwards

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
flatulence is gas, also called wind

explanation.surface: A treacherous person hiding in the grass is on the point of passing gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snake in the grass' wants to be the definition, but 'grass' is needed as fodder; 'about' makes SIDEER and 'to admit' takes the gas inside. 'in the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidewinder is a small desert rattlesnake that moves sideways in loops.

clue.text: Where boy is brought up in North America — the Sagebrush State

indicators.note: the turned name goes inside the abbreviation
in a down clue, bringing something up reads it bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: Dave is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A question about where a boy was raised in North America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' makes EVAD, a down-clue reversal; 'in' houses it. 'Where' and 'is' are links, and the surface reads as a question about a boy's upbringing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagebrush State is the official nickname of this US state.

clue.text: Old instrument made from wood found in street

indicators.note: being found in something means sitting inside it

parts.note: pine is a wood

explanation.surface: An antique keyboard made of timber is discovered on a street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made from' is a link; 'found in' houses the timber, and 'Old instrument' is the definition despite 'made from wood' sounding like its description.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinet is a small harpsichord, an old keyboard instrument.

clue.text: See 10
After round after round, yearn for tea

indicators.note: the second round piece follows the first
the word for yearn comes after the two round pieces

parts.note: a round shape looks like the letter O
a second round shape gives another letter O
to yearn for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: After many rounds of drinks, someone wants a cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a pub crawl; the two O shapes come first, then LONG.
explanation.definitionFit: Oolong is a partly fermented Chinese tea, between green and black.

clue.text: It's safe to excoriate Barrie's work

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe
to excoriate is to criticise harshly, which is to pan

explanation.surface: A claim that it is fine to tear apart a playwright's work.
explanation.walkthrough: PETER is old thieves' slang for a safe, a useful crossword convention. 'It's' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: J. M. Barrie wrote the play about the boy who never grows up.

clue.text: Set up home music centre initially, then actually listen

parts.note: being at home is being in

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter, here of music
the initial letters of the three following words are taken

explanation.surface: Installing a home stereo and then actually listening to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'music centre' looks like a hi-fi unit, but gives the middle letter S of 'music'; 'initially' takes T, A, L.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a variant spelling of the verb meaning to put equipment in place and connect it.

clue.text: English composer holding recipe that may be used in kitchen

definitions.text: that may be used in kitchen

indicators.note: holding means containing, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Sir John Stainer was an English Victorian composer of church music
R is an abbreviation for recipe, as on prescriptions

explanation.surface: An English composer has a recipe for use in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: R for recipe comes from the Latin 'recipe' (take) written on prescriptions.
explanation.definitionFit: A sieve or colander for draining food is a kitchen utensil.

clue.text: They tend the sick sharks

definitions.meaning: people who care for patients in hospital
a kind of shark that lives on the sea floor in warm waters

explanation.surface: Hospital carers are compared to predatory fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Hospital carers have this name, and so does a family of slow bottom-dwelling sharks.

clue.text: Roving reporter's first meeting with gunners in lane between houses

indicators.note: the two letters go inside the lane

parts.note: in northern England an entry is a narrow passage between houses

indicators.note: the first letter of the word reporter's is taken

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners

explanation.surface: A roaming journalist meets some artillerymen in a back alley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meeting with' joins the reporter's initial and the artillery; 'in' houses them. 'Roving reporter' reads as one phrase, but 'Roving' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Errantry is the wandering life of a knight-errant, so roving is its sense.
